Today Freya Axelsen had every chance of setting a new record. Right now three hundred and fifty thousand people were watching her stream, and the number was climbing fast, because the broadcast was moving into the Q&A segment.

If the live audience hit four hundred thousand, it would be an absolute world record for the entire coaching industry.

No one had ever managed it. Even the famous and indecently rich Tony Robbins, in his prime, had drawn only three hundred and ninety thousand, and that after decades in the business and with a face the whole world knew! Now Freya had a chance to blow through that ceiling with room to spare and secure her fame for years to come. And if anyone thought this was just dumb luck, Freya knew better: fortune smiles only on prepared minds and hands ready to act.

At first it had all gone merely fine. The first hour was a lecture on how to achieve your goals. It was the most enjoyable part, but only a hundred thousand showed up. Expected, but not up to Freya's level, with her four million followers on Instagram and another twelve million on TikTok. Freya didn't like the latter for its lack of a serious audience, but the algorithms had decided otherwise.

Another hour went to questions along the lines of "the best age to found a startup" and "how to get up and start doing things," which subscribers had left through the stream's submission form. The questions landed well and pulled the viewer count up to two hundred thousand.

But that was still not enough. It was a plateau. Two hundred thousand was a plateau, and each time it got harder to break through.

And then Freya went all in, as New York dealmakers like to say. Within twenty minutes, right in the middle of the stream, her assistants bolted on a payment form and wrote the social media posts. And the surprise part of the broadcast began: open questions in exchange for donations. No moderation, but on Freya's terms.

changes.after: open questions in exchange for donations
